sentences.text: Pepsico India Holding Pvt. Ltd. vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
on 21 November, 2019

Author: Vishal Dhagat
Bench: Vishal Dhagat
 1 
 The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 Mcrc-5233-2018
 (Pepsico India Holding Pvt. Ltd. Vs The State Of Madhya 
 12
 Jabalpur, Dated : 21-11-2019
 Shri Surendra Singh, senior counsel with Shri Abhisekh Arja
 Advocate for the petitioner.
Shri Rohit Sohgaura, learned Govt. Advocate for the respond Complainant, Food Inspector, has filed complaint under Sections 2, 7 and 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
On 05.12.2009 Food Inspector purchased packets of product Kurkure along with other food articles.
Packet was send for examination at State Food Laboratory.
Public Analyst examined the product on 30.12.2009 and submitted report on 11.01.2010.
Manufacturing date of product was 21.11.2009 and product was best before 4 months i.e. till 20.03.2010.
Visible extraneous matter present and product Kurkure Masala Munch was found to be adulterated.
Deputy Director, Food and Drug Administration gave sanction for prosecution on 21.02.2011.
Notice to petitioner company was issued on 28.10.2010 under Section 14 (A) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

It is submitted by learned Senior Counsel appearing for petitioner that product has crossed its shelf life of 4 months i.e. 20.03.2010 and the same could not be send for re-analysis and notices were received after its best before date.
Thus, there is denial of right of re-analysis which is fatal to the prosecution case.
Learned Senior Counsel placed reliance on 2015 (2) FAC 441, 2019 (2) FAC 58.
Heard the arguments of both the parties.
Considering the complaint and documents filed along with it.
It is clear that complaint was filed after shelf life of the product and valuable rights of 2 MCRC-5233-2018 petitioner under Section 13 (2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 is violated.
